subject: physics_2
question_text: State and explain Coulomb's inverse square law in electricity.

verification.note: The 1+2+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: F = (1/4πε₀)·Q₁Q₂/r² with k = 1/4πε₀ = 9 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²; in a medium ε = ε₀εᵣ replaces ε₀. The book prints 'permitivity of free spaced' and 'electrostalic' (printed p.19-20); written correctly here.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The statement
lines: The force of attraction or repulsion
between two stationary point charges is
directly proportional to the product of the
square of the distance between them, and
acts along the line joining the two
steps.margin_note: First mark. Three parts: product of charges, inverse square of distance, along the joining line.
steps.why: The statement has three separate claims and the examiner checks all three. Stationary and point-sized matter too — the law is stated for point charges at rest.
common_mistakes: Leaving out acts along the line joining the charges — the direction is part of the law.
Writing proportional to the sum of the charges. It is the PRODUCT Q₁Q₂.

recall.must_convey: That the force is proportional to the product of the charges, inversely proportional to the square of the distance, and acts along the joining line.
reject: one by four pi epsilon nought

steps.memory_tip: Three claims in one sentence: product, inverse square, joining line.

steps.label: The figure
steps.margin_note: Two point charges Q₁ and Q₂, a distance r apart. Draw it beside the explanation — it defines the symbols the formula uses.
steps.why: The figure fixes what Q₁, Q₂ and r mean before they appear in the formula, so the explanation reads as geometry instead of as symbols from nowhere.
common_mistakes: Marking r from the surfaces of two large bodies. The law is for POINT charges, r is between the points.

recall.must_convey: That the figure shows two point charges Q₁ and Q₂ separated by a distance r.
accept: draw two charges a distance r apart
mark Q one, Q two and r
reject: F equals k Q1 Q2 by r squared

steps.memory_tip: Two dots, one line, one letter r — the whole law lives on this picture.

Here ε₀ is the permittivity of free space.
steps.margin_note: Two marks. One for the proportionality made into an equation, one for k = 1/4πε₀ with its value.
steps.why: The explanation is the statement turned into symbols: the two proportionalities combine into one, and the constant k carries the units. Naming ε₀ as the permittivity of free space shows where k comes from.
common_mistakes: Quoting k as 9 × 10⁹ with no unit. The unit N m² C⁻² is part of the value.
Writing r instead of r² in the denominator.

recall.must_convey: That F = (1/4πε₀) · Q₁Q₂/r², with k = 1/4πε₀ = 9 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻².
accept: F equals one by four pi epsilon nought into Q1 Q2 by r squared

steps.memory_tip: Proportionality first, then k, then k's value — three lines, two marks.

steps.label: Force in a medium
lines: If the charges are placed in a material
medium of permittivity ε = ε₀εᵣ, the force
where εᵣ is the relative permittivity of
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Replace ε₀ by ε = ε₀εᵣ — the force in a medium is smaller by the factor εᵣ.
steps.why: The medium form is the same law with ε₀ replaced by ε. Since εᵣ > 1 for every material medium, the force between the same charges is smaller inside a medium than in free space.
common_mistakes: Writing ε = ε₀ + εᵣ. The permittivity multiplies: ε = ε₀εᵣ.
Saying the force increases in a medium. εᵣ > 1, so the force decreases.

recall.must_convey: That in a medium ε = ε₀εᵣ replaces ε₀, so the force becomes smaller.
accept: epsilon equals epsilon nought epsilon r
reject: k is nine into ten power nine

steps.memory_tip: Same law, bigger permittivity, smaller force — divide by εᵣ.

insider_note: The middle two marks are the explanation — the proportionality turned into an equation and k given with both its form and its value; the medium line is the mark most students never write.
